topics.name: ICU Neuromonitoring
topics.blurb: Bedside intracranial, metabolic, and electrophysiologic monitoring and CSF diversion management in the neuro-ICU.

topics.name: Sodium and Endocrine Disorders
topics.blurb: Dysnatremia, pituitary axis disturbance, and osmotherapy of the neurocritically ill.

topics.name: Seizures and Status Epilepticus
topics.blurb: ICU seizure recognition, status escalation, prophylaxis, and antiepileptic management.

topics.name: Airway and Ventilation
topics.blurb: Neuro-specific intubation, ventilation targets, and tracheostomy/extubation decisions.

topics.name: Hemodynamics and Cardiac Complications
topics.blurb: Blood-pressure and perfusion management plus neurogenic cardiopulmonary complications.

topics.name: Sedation, Analgesia, and Delirium
topics.blurb: Sedative/analgesic selection preserving the neuro exam, paralysis, and delirium control.

topics.name: Temperature Management
topics.blurb: Fever burden, targeted temperature management, and shivering control.

topics.name: Hematology and Thromboprophylaxis
topics.blurb: VTE prophylaxis timing, transfusion thresholds, reversal, and ICU coagulopathy.

topics.name: CNS Infection in the ICU
topics.blurb: Ventriculitis, healthcare-associated meningitis, antibiotic CSF penetration, and surgical site infection.

topics.name: Brain Death and Prognostication
topics.blurb: Death by neurologic criteria, organ donation pathways, and coma prognostication.

topics.name: Nutrition and Metabolic Support
topics.blurb: Early feeding, glucose targets, and stress-ulcer prophylaxis.

topics.name: Dysautonomia
topics.blurb: Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity recognition and control.

topics.name: Disorders of Consciousness and Rehabilitation
topics.blurb: Consciousness scales, recovery pharmacology, and ICU-to-rehab transitions.

concepts.name: EVD setup, leveling, and zeroing
concepts.blurb: Level the transducer to the tragus/foramen of Monro and zero so drainage pressure and ICP read accurately.
acgme: External Ventricular Drain (EVD) Placement and Management

concepts.name: EVD weaning and clamp trial
concepts.blurb: Raise drain height then clamp while watching ICP and exam to test whether CSF diversion can be removed.
acgme: External Ventricular Drain (EVD) Placement and Management

concepts.name: EVD infection prevention
concepts.blurb: Sterile insertion, antibiotic-impregnated catheters, closed systems, and minimizing CSF sampling lower ventriculostomy infection rates.
acgme: Surgical Site Infection in Neurosurgery - Prevention Diagnosis and Treatment

concepts.name: Lumbar drain management
concepts.blurb: Controlled lumbar CSF diversion for leaks and SAH; contraindicated with obstructive hydrocephalus or mass effect risking herniation.
acgme: Lumbar Drain Placement - Technique Indications and Complications

concepts.name: Parenchymal ICP monitor vs EVD
concepts.blurb: Intraparenchymal bolts measure but cannot drain and may drift; EVD both measures and treats but carries infection risk.
acgme: ICP Monitoring - Parenchymal Monitor Placement and Interpretation

concepts.name: Indications for ICP monitoring
concepts.blurb: Monitor severe TBI with abnormal CT, or normal CT plus age/posturing/hypotension risk factors, per Brain Trauma Foundation.
acgme: ICP Monitoring - Parenchymal Monitor Placement and Interpretation

concepts.name: ICP waveform and plateau waves
concepts.blurb: Rising P2 above P1 signals poor compliance; Lundberg A (plateau) waves indicate exhausted compensatory reserve.
acgme: ICP Monitoring - Parenchymal Monitor Placement and Interpretation

concepts.name: Brain tissue oxygen monitoring
concepts.blurb: PbtO2 probe detects regional hypoxia; values below ~20 mmHg prompt oxygenation, perfusion, or transfusion interventions.
acgme: Cerebral Metabolism Monitoring - Jugular Bulb O2 Brain PO2 (Licox) Microdialysis

concepts.name: Jugular venous oximetry
concepts.blurb: SjvO2 reflects global oxygen extraction; low values suggest hypoperfusion, high values hyperemia or infarction.
acgme: Cerebral Metabolism Monitoring - Jugular Bulb O2 Brain PO2 (Licox) Microdialysis

concepts.name: Cerebral microdialysis
concepts.blurb: Samples brain interstitium; a rising lactate-pyruvate ratio with low glucose signals metabolic crisis before ICP rises.
acgme: Cerebral Metabolism Monitoring - Jugular Bulb O2 Brain PO2 (Licox) Microdialysis

concepts.name: Continuous EEG indications
concepts.blurb: cEEG detects nonconvulsive seizures in unexplained altered consciousness, after convulsive status, and in poor-grade SAH/TBI.
acgme: Status Epilepticus - Recognition and Treatment Protocol

concepts.name: Transcranial Doppler in the ICU
concepts.blurb: Bedside flow velocities trend vasospasm after SAH; high MCA velocity with elevated Lindegaard ratio distinguishes spasm from hyperemia.
acgme: Cerebral Vasospasm and Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After SAH

concepts.name: Quantitative pupillometry
concepts.blurb: Automated pupillometry yields a Neurological Pupil index; falling NPi can precede herniation before manual exam detects change.
acgme: ICP Monitoring - Parenchymal Monitor Placement and Interpretation

concepts.name: Autoregulation monitoring and optimal CPP
concepts.blurb: The pressure reactivity index correlates ICP with MAP to derive a patient-specific optimal CPP target.
acgme: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure - CPP MAP - ICP Targets and Optimization

concepts.name: Multimodal monitoring integration
concepts.blurb: Integrate ICP, CPP, PbtO2, microdialysis, and EEG to detect secondary injury and individualize therapy, not chase isolated numbers.
acgme: Cerebral Metabolism Monitoring - Jugular Bulb O2 Brain PO2 (Licox) Microdialysis

concepts.name: CSF overdrainage and complications
concepts.blurb: Excess CSF drainage risks slit ventricles, upward/downward herniation, subdural hematoma, and ventricular collapse around the catheter.
acgme: External Ventricular Drain (EVD) Placement and Management

concepts.name: Hyponatremia diagnostic algorithm
concepts.blurb: Assess serum/urine osmolality, urine sodium, and volume status to classify hypotonic hyponatremia before treating.
acgme: Fluids and Electrolytes in Neurosurgery - Na K Mg Ca Targets

concepts.name: SIADH
concepts.blurb: Inappropriate ADH causes euvolemic hyponatremia with concentrated urine; managed by fluid restriction, not saline loading.
acgme: Sodium Disorders in Neurocritical Care - SIADH vs CSW - Diagnosis and Treatment

concepts.name: Cerebral salt wasting
concepts.blurb: Renal sodium loss causes hypovolemic hyponatremia after SAH/brain injury; treated with salt and volume repletion.
acgme: Sodium Disorders in Neurocritical Care - SIADH vs CSW - Diagnosis and Treatment

concepts.name: SIADH versus cerebral salt wasting
concepts.blurb: Volume status is the discriminator: SIADH is euvolemic and fluid-restricted, CSW is hypovolemic and volume-repleted.
acgme: Sodium Disorders in Neurocritical Care - SIADH vs CSW - Diagnosis and Treatment

concepts.name: Central diabetes insipidus
concepts.blurb: ADH deficiency causes dilute polyuria and hypernatremia after pituitary/skull-base surgery or brain death; treat with desmopressin.
acgme: Diabetes Insipidus - Post-Pituitary or Skull Base Surgery and TBI

concepts.name: Triple-phase response
concepts.blurb: Post-pituitary injury cycles through transient DI, then SIADH-like ADH release, then permanent DI, demanding dynamic management.
acgme: Diabetes Insipidus - Post-Pituitary or Skull Base Surgery and TBI

concepts.name: Hypertonic saline protocols
concepts.blurb: Bolus or infusion of 3%-23.4% saline raises serum sodium for ICP control or symptomatic hyponatremia with set correction limits.
acgme: Osmotherapy - Mannitol vs Hypertonic Saline - Mechanisms and Targets

concepts.name: Osmotic demyelination syndrome
concepts.blurb: Overrapid correction of chronic hyponatremia causes central pontine myelinolysis; limit rise to roughly 6-8 mEq/L per day.
acgme: Sodium Disorders in Neurocritical Care - SIADH vs CSW - Diagnosis and Treatment

concepts.name: Stress-dose steroids and adrenal axis
concepts.blurb: Suspect secondary adrenal insufficiency after pituitary surgery or chronic steroids; give stress-dose hydrocortisone for hypotension.
acgme: Fluids and Electrolytes in Neurosurgery - Na K Mg Ca Targets

concepts.name: Hypernatremia management
concepts.blurb: Replace free-water deficit slowly while distinguishing iatrogenic osmotherapy-driven hypernatremia from DI-driven water loss.
acgme: Fluids and Electrolytes in Neurosurgery - Na K Mg Ca Targets

concepts.name: Nonconvulsive status epilepticus
concepts.blurb: Persistent altered consciousness without overt convulsions; diagnosed on EEG and a common cause of unexplained coma in the ICU.
acgme: Status Epilepticus - Recognition and Treatment Protocol

concepts.name: NCSE versus encephalopathy
concepts.blurb: Distinguish seizures from metabolic encephalopathy using EEG criteria; ictal-interictal patterns may need a benzodiazepine trial.
acgme: Status Epilepticus - Recognition and Treatment Protocol

concepts.name: ICU EEG patterns and Salzburg criteria
concepts.blurb: Periodic discharges and rhythmic patterns occupy an ictal-interictal continuum; Salzburg criteria define electrographic status.
acgme: Status Epilepticus - Recognition and Treatment Protocol

concepts.name: Status epilepticus escalation algorithm
concepts.blurb: Benzodiazepine first line, then a second-line AED load, then anesthetic infusion for refractory status, on a time-driven ladder.
acgme: Status Epilepticus - Recognition and Treatment Protocol

concepts.name: Refractory and super-refractory status
concepts.blurb: Status failing two agents needs continuous midazolam, propofol, or pentobarbital titrated to EEG seizure or burst suppression.
acgme: Status Epilepticus - Recognition and Treatment Protocol

concepts.name: AED loading and serum levels
concepts.blurb: Load levetiracetam, fosphenytoin, or valproate by weight; follow free phenytoin levels and watch hypotension during fast infusion.
acgme: Antiepileptic Drug Pharmacology - Mechanisms and Interactions

concepts.name: Post-craniotomy seizure prophylaxis
concepts.blurb: Evidence supports only a short early-seizure prophylaxis course after craniotomy or TBI, not prolonged AED therapy.
acgme: Antiepileptic Drug Pharmacology - Mechanisms and Interactions

concepts.name: Neuroprotective intubation
concepts.blurb: Avoid hypotension and hypoxia during RSI, blunt the ICP response, and maintain cervical precautions in trauma.
acgme: Airway Management - RSI Indications Technique and Failed Airway Protocol

concepts.name: Induction agents for the brain-injured
concepts.blurb: Choose hemodynamically neutral induction; etomidate and ketamine preserve pressure, and ketamine does not meaningfully raise ICP.
acgme: Airway Management - RSI Indications Technique and Failed Airway Protocol

concepts.name: Ventilation targets in brain injury
concepts.blurb: Maintain normocapnia (PaCO2 35-40) and adequate oxygenation; both hypo- and hypercapnia worsen secondary injury.
acgme: Mechanical Ventilation in Neurocritical Care - Targets Modes Weaning

concepts.name: Hyperventilation use and harms
concepts.blurb: Brief hyperventilation lowers ICP via vasoconstriction but risks ischemia; reserve for herniation as a bridge, not sustained therapy.
acgme: Mechanical Ventilation in Neurocritical Care - Targets Modes Weaning

concepts.name: PEEP and intracranial pressure
concepts.blurb: PEEP can raise ICP by impeding cerebral venous outflow, but moderate levels are usually safe and improve oxygenation.
acgme: Mechanical Ventilation in Neurocritical Care - Targets Modes Weaning

concepts.name: ARDS in the brain-injured patient
concepts.blurb: Balance lung-protective low tidal volumes and permissive hypercapnia against ICP control; prone positioning complicates monitoring.
acgme: Mechanical Ventilation in Neurocritical Care - Targets Modes Weaning

concepts.name: Tracheostomy timing
concepts.blurb: Early tracheostomy in patients unlikely to extubate may reduce ventilator days; severe injury predicts prolonged airway need.
acgme: Tracheostomy - Percutaneous Dilatational and Open Surgical Technique

concepts.name: Extubation with poor mental status
concepts.blurb: Low GCS alone need not preclude extubation; airway protection, secretions, cough, and oxygenation predict success better.
acgme: Mechanical Ventilation in Neurocritical Care - Targets Modes Weaning

concepts.name: MAP and CPP augmentation
concepts.blurb: Raise MAP with fluids and vasopressors to keep CPP roughly 60-70 mmHg, avoiding both ischemia and ARDS from overshoot.
acgme: Cerebral Perfusion Pressure - CPP MAP - ICP Targets and Optimization

concepts.name: Vasopressor selection for neuro patients
concepts.blurb: Norepinephrine is first-line for cerebral perfusion; phenylephrine suits tachyarrhythmia, vasopressin spares catecholamine dosing.
acgme: Neurogenic Shock - Spinal Cord Injury - MAP Goals Vasopressors Fluids

concepts.name: Neurogenic shock management
concepts.blurb: Spinal cord injury causes hypotension with bradycardia from sympathetic loss; treat with fluids, vasopressors, and MAP goals.
acgme: Neurogenic Shock - Spinal Cord Injury - MAP Goals Vasopressors Fluids

concepts.name: Blood pressure management after ICH
concepts.blurb: Acutely lower systolic toward ~140 mmHg in spontaneous ICH to limit hematoma expansion, avoiding rapid overcorrection.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: Blood pressure management in SAH
concepts.blurb: Before securing the aneurysm avoid hypertension to limit rebleeding; afterward permit higher pressure to counter delayed ischemia.
acgme: Cerebral Vasospasm and Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After SAH

concepts.name: Hypertensive emergency control
concepts.blurb: Use titratable agents like nicardipine or clevidipine for smooth control; avoid nitroprusside/nitroglycerin that raise ICP.
acgme: Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage - Medical and Surgical Management

concepts.name: Neurogenic stunned myocardium
concepts.blurb: Catecholamine surge after SAH/TBI causes takotsubo-pattern dysfunction with troponin rise and wall-motion abnormalities, usually reversible.
acgme: Neurogenic Cardiac Complications (Takotsubo Arrhythmias in SAH and TBI)

concepts.name: Neurogenic pulmonary edema
concepts.blurb: Acute catecholamine-driven capillary leak causes pulmonary edema after severe brain injury; supportive ventilation while treating the brain.
acgme: Neurogenic Cardiac Complications (Takotsubo Arrhythmias in SAH and TBI)

concepts.name: ECG changes and arrhythmia in SAH
concepts.blurb: SAH produces cerebral T-wave inversions, QT prolongation, and arrhythmias from autonomic storm rather than primary coronary disease.
acgme: Neurogenic Cardiac Complications (Takotsubo Arrhythmias in SAH and TBI)

concepts.name: Fluid management and euvolemia
concepts.blurb: Maintain euvolemia with isotonic fluids; hypotonic solutions worsen cerebral edema and overly negative balance risks hypoperfusion.
acgme: Fluids and Electrolytes in Neurosurgery - Na K Mg Ca Targets

concepts.name: Sedation preserving the neuro exam
concepts.blurb: Favor short-acting sedation with scheduled awakening windows so neurologic deterioration is not masked.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Propofol versus dexmedetomidine
concepts.blurb: Propofol allows rapid titration and burst suppression; dexmedetomidine gives arousable sedation without respiratory depression.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Dexmedetomidine
concepts.blurb: Central alpha-2 agonist giving cooperative sedation and analgesia sparing; causes bradycardia and hypotension, not respiratory depression.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Propofol infusion syndrome
concepts.blurb: High-dose prolonged propofol causes lactic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hyperkalemia, and cardiac failure; limit dose and duration.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Barbiturate coma for refractory ICP
concepts.blurb: Pentobarbital titrated to EEG burst suppression lowers cerebral metabolism for refractory intracranial hypertension, risking hypotension and infection.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Neuromuscular blockade in the neuro-ICU
concepts.blurb: Paralytics control shivering, ICP, and ventilator dyssynchrony but mask seizures and the exam; always pair with deep sedation.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Analgesia-first sedation
concepts.blurb: Treat pain first with opioids or multimodal agents, since untreated pain raises ICP, agitation, and sedative requirements.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Sedation scales and targeted depth
concepts.blurb: Use RASS-guided light sedation with daily interruption to reduce ventilator days, unless ICP or status requires deep sedation.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: ICU delirium
concepts.blurb: Screen with CAM-ICU; prevent with light sedation, mobility, sleep, and benzodiazepine avoidance more than antipsychotic treatment.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Ketamine in neurocritical care
concepts.blurb: Ketamine preserves hemodynamics and analgesia and does not meaningfully raise ICP, countering the older avoidance dogma.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Fever burden and secondary injury
concepts.blurb: Fever increases cerebral metabolic demand and worsens outcomes after brain injury, making normothermia a therapeutic target.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Central versus infectious fever
concepts.blurb: Diagnose central fever only after excluding infection, drug, and thrombosis; SAH and IVH predispose to noninfectious fever.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Targeted temperature management
concepts.blurb: Controlled normothermia or mild hypothermia after cardiac arrest; evidence favors fever avoidance over deep cooling for neuroprotection.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Therapeutic hypothermia for ICP
concepts.blurb: Hypothermia lowers refractory ICP but EUROTHERM showed worse outcomes, so it is a salvage rather than routine therapy.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: Shivering management
concepts.blurb: Shivering raises metabolic demand and counters cooling; control with surface counterwarming, magnesium, buspirone, opioids, then paralysis.
acgme: ICP Management After TBI - Tiered Protocol Osmotherapy Cooling

concepts.name: VTE chemoprophylaxis timing
concepts.blurb: Start pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis after craniotomy or ICH once imaging shows hemorrhage stability, typically 24-72 hours.
acgme: DVT or PE Prophylaxis in Neurosurgery - Timing Risk Stratification

concepts.name: Mechanical VTE prophylaxis
concepts.blurb: Intermittent pneumatic compression starts on admission and bridges until chemoprophylaxis is safe after intracranial hemorrhage.
acgme: DVT or PE Prophylaxis in Neurosurgery - Timing Risk Stratification

concepts.name: VTE treatment with intracranial bleeding
concepts.blurb: When anticoagulation is contraindicated by fresh hemorrhage, place a retrievable IVC filter, then transition to anticoagulation when safe.
acgme: DVT or PE Prophylaxis in Neurosurgery - Timing Risk Stratification

concepts.name: Platelet thresholds for procedures
concepts.blurb: Target roughly 100k for craniotomy or EVD and at least 50k for lumbar puncture; correct dysfunction from antiplatelet drugs.
acgme: Coagulopathy Reversal in Neurosurgery - Warfarin NOAC Antiplatelet Reversal

concepts.name: Transfusion thresholds
concepts.blurb: A restrictive hemoglobin trigger near 7 g/dL suits most patients, though brain injury with low PbtO2 may warrant higher targets.
acgme: Fluids and Electrolytes in Neurosurgery - Na K Mg Ca Targets

concepts.name: Anticoagulation reversal in hemorrhage
concepts.blurb: Reverse warfarin with 4-factor PCC and vitamin K, dabigatran with idarucizumab, and factor Xa inhibitors with andexanet or PCC.
acgme: Coagulopathy Reversal in Neurosurgery - Warfarin NOAC Antiplatelet Reversal

concepts.name: Anticoagulation resumption timing
concepts.blurb: Balance rebleeding against thrombosis when restarting anticoagulation after ICH; timing depends on indication and bleed stability.
acgme: Coagulopathy Reversal in Neurosurgery - Warfarin NOAC Antiplatelet Reversal

concepts.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation
concepts.blurb: Severe TBI releases tissue factor triggering consumptive coagulopathy with prolonged times, low fibrinogen, and microvascular thrombosis.
acgme: Coagulopathy Reversal in Neurosurgery - Warfarin NOAC Antiplatelet Reversal

concepts.name: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
concepts.blurb: Antibody-mediated platelet activation causing paradoxical thrombosis days into heparin; stop heparin and use a non-heparin anticoagulant.
acgme: DVT or PE Prophylaxis in Neurosurgery - Timing Risk Stratification

concepts.name: Ventriculitis diagnosis and CSF profile
concepts.blurb: Drain-associated ventriculitis shows falling CSF glucose, rising protein and cell count, and positive cultures; trends matter more than single values.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Ventriculitis versus chemical meningitis
concepts.blurb: Blood or surgery can cause sterile CSF pleocytosis; positive culture, persistently low glucose, and clinical course distinguish true infection.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Healthcare-associated meningitis
concepts.blurb: Post-neurosurgical meningitis is driven by staphylococci and gram-negative rods, demanding broader empiric cover than community disease.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Community-acquired meningitis management
concepts.blurb: Give empiric vancomycin plus ceftriaxone with adjunctive dexamethasone urgently; do not delay antibiotics for imaging or LP.
acgme: Meningitis and Encephalitis - Diagnosis Empiric Treatment and LP Interpretation

concepts.name: Empiric regimen for CNS infection
concepts.blurb: For nosocomial CNS infection start vancomycin plus an antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime/meropenem), then narrow by culture.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Antibiotic CSF penetration
concepts.blurb: Penetration depends on lipophilicity, protein binding, and meningeal inflammation; dose to maximize CSF levels for cure.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Intraventricular antibiotic therapy
concepts.blurb: Intraventricular vancomycin or aminoglycosides via EVD treat ventriculitis refractory to systemic therapy when CSF levels are inadequate.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: Shunt and drain infection management
concepts.blurb: Infected hardware usually requires removal, external drainage, antibiotics until CSF clears, then reimplantation.
acgme: VP Shunt Failure and Complications - Mechanical Obstruction Infection Over-drainage

concepts.name: Surgical site infection
concepts.blurb: Wound infection, bone-flap osteomyelitis, and subgaleal abscess present subacutely; prevention uses prophylactic antibiotics and glycemic control.
acgme: Surgical Site Infection in Neurosurgery - Prevention Diagnosis and Treatment

concepts.name: Brain death determination prerequisites
concepts.blurb: Confirm irreversible catastrophic injury and exclude confounders: normothermia, normotension, no sedatives, and corrected metabolic derangement.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Confounders of brain death exam
concepts.blurb: Hypothermia, sedatives, neuromuscular blockade, severe acid-base or electrolyte derangement, and shock all invalidate the exam until corrected.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Brain death clinical examination
concepts.blurb: Document coma, absent brainstem reflexes across all levels, and no motor response, confirming whole-brain unresponsiveness.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Apnea testing
concepts.blurb: Preoxygenate, disconnect, and confirm no respiratory effort despite PaCO2 rising above 60 mmHg or 20 above baseline.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Ancillary tests for brain death
concepts.blurb: When apnea testing or exam cannot be completed, use cerebral angiography, nuclear flow, or EEG to confirm absent function/flow.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Spinally mediated reflexes
concepts.blurb: Spinal reflexes and the Lazarus sign can persist after brain death and do not invalidate the determination.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Brain death versus coma and mimics
concepts.blurb: Distinguish brain death from coma, persistent vegetative state, and locked-in syndrome, where some brain function and reflexes persist.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Donation after brain death
concepts.blurb: After declaration, organ-procurement organizations lead donor management to preserve organ perfusion; the care team avoids conflict of interest.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Donation after circulatory death
concepts.blurb: DCD follows planned withdrawal in patients not meeting brain death, with procurement after a defined no-touch circulatory arrest interval.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Withdrawal of care and goals discussions
concepts.blurb: Lead family meetings aligning prognosis with patient values, avoiding premature withdrawal driven by self-fulfilling prognostic pessimism.
acgme: Prognostication in Severe TBI - IMPACT Model Withdrawal of Care Discussions

concepts.name: Coma prognostication after cardiac arrest
concepts.blurb: Use multimodal data (exam, SSEP, EEG, NSE, imaging) at least 72 hours off sedation and after rewarming before prognosticating.
acgme: Prognostication in Severe TBI - IMPACT Model Withdrawal of Care Discussions

concepts.name: Early enteral nutrition
concepts.blurb: Start enteral feeding within 24-72 hours in brain-injured patients, who are hypermetabolic and benefit from early caloric delivery.
acgme: Enteral Nutrition and Gastrostomy (PEG) in Long-Term Neurosurgical Patients

concepts.name: Nutrition needs and hypermetabolism
concepts.blurb: Severe brain injury drives catabolic hypermetabolism; estimate elevated caloric and protein needs and plan PEG for prolonged dysphagia.
acgme: Enteral Nutrition and Gastrostomy (PEG) in Long-Term Neurosurgical Patients

concepts.name: Glucose targets in brain injury
concepts.blurb: Avoid both hyperglycemia and tight control; target roughly 140-180 mg/dL since hypoglycemia worsens brain metabolic crisis.
acgme: Fluids and Electrolytes in Neurosurgery - Na K Mg Ca Targets

concepts.name: Stress-ulcer prophylaxis
concepts.blurb: Give acid suppression to mechanically ventilated or coagulopathic patients, balancing GI-bleed prevention against pneumonia and C. difficile risk.
acgme: Enteral Nutrition and Gastrostomy (PEG) in Long-Term Neurosurgical Patients

concepts.name: Paroxysmal sympathetic hyperactivity
concepts.blurb: Episodic tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, diaphoresis, and posturing after severe TBI from disinhibited sympathetic discharge.
acgme: Diffuse Axonal Injury - Pathophysiology MRI Susceptibility Imaging Prognosis

concepts.name: PSH versus sepsis and seizures
concepts.blurb: PSH is a diagnosis of exclusion; rule out infection, seizures, pulmonary embolism, pain, and withdrawal before attributing storms to dysautonomia.
acgme: Sepsis and CNS Infection in the ICU - Meningitis Ventriculitis Abscess

concepts.name: PSH management
concepts.blurb: Abort episodes and reduce frequency with opioids, beta-blockers, gabapentin, clonidine, and bromocriptine while limiting triggers.
acgme: Sedation and Analgesia in Neurocritical Care - Propofol Dexmedetomidine Fentanyl

concepts.name: Disorders of consciousness classification
concepts.blurb: Distinguish coma, vegetative/unresponsive wakefulness, and minimally conscious state by arousal and reproducible awareness behaviors.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Coma Recovery Scale-Revised
concepts.blurb: The CRS-R standardizes serial assessment across auditory, visual, motor, and communication subscales to detect minimal consciousness.
acgme: Brain Death - Clinical Determination and Confirmatory Testing

concepts.name: Amantadine for recovery of consciousness
concepts.blurb: Randomized evidence shows amantadine accelerates functional recovery in post-traumatic disorders of consciousness.
acgme: Prognostication in Severe TBI - IMPACT Model Withdrawal of Care Discussions

concepts.name: Early mobilization and rehab transition
concepts.blurb: Early physical therapy and structured ICU-to-rehab transition reduce ICU-acquired weakness and delirium and improve functional outcomes.
acgme: Enteral Nutrition and Gastrostomy (PEG) in Long-Term Neurosurgical Patients
